items.text: Understand why private subnets need NAT — private IPs aren't routable on the internet
Explain what NAT Gateway is and its key features (managed, auto-scales to 45 Gbps, Elastic IP required)
Explain what NAT Instance is and when it might be chosen over NAT Gateway
Understand Source/Destination Check and why it must be disabled for NAT Instance
Describe Site-to-Site VPN components: VGW (AWS side) and CGW (customer side)
Understand AWS Direct Connect — dedicated fiber, bypasses internet, not encrypted by default
Explain the difference between VPN and Direct Connect (latency, bandwidth, cost, setup time)
Understand Transit Gateway as a central hub for multi-VPC and hybrid connectivity
Can create a NAT Gateway in the correct (public) subnet and assign an Elastic IP
Can update a private subnet route table to route 0.0.0.0/0 through a NAT Gateway
Can explain the correct setup order for Site-to-Site VPN (VGW → CGW → VPN Connection)
Can navigate the VPC console to find VPN and Direct Connect options
Can design a multi-AZ NAT Gateway architecture for high availability
Can recommend VPN vs Direct Connect based on a given scenario's requirements
Recall NAT Gateway is managed, auto-scales to 45 Gbps, requires Elastic IP
Recall NAT Instance requires Source/Destination Check disabled
Recall that for HA, one NAT Gateway per AZ is needed (not one per VPC)
Recall VPN tunnel bandwidth limit is ~1.25 Gbps and uses IPSec encryption
Recall Direct Connect is NOT encrypted by default — must add VPN for encryption
Recall Direct Connect takes weeks to provision while VPN takes hours
Can answer: 'When would you use VPN vs Direct Connect?' correctly in an exam scenario
